name: Tokio 7
blurb: Long-running designer consignment in a basement space; strong on Japanese labels and archive runway pieces.

name: AuH2O Thriftique
blurb: Tightly packed thrift-priced racks with a punk and party-dress bent. Owner-curated rather than donation-sorted.

name: Village Style
blurb: Dense basement vintage; denim, leather, band tees and workwear stacked to the ceiling.

name: Trash and Vaudeville
blurb: East Village punk institution since 1975. Mostly new reproduction rather than true vintage, but the reason half the block still dresses this way.
notes: Mostly new stock - included for context; flag if you want vintage-only

name: Search & Destroy
blurb: Studs, tartan, customized leather and secondhand punk on a wall of pinned-up stock.

name: Metropolis Vintage
blurb: Broad general vintage: tees, western shirts, varsity jackets, sunglasses. A good first stop for orientation.

name: Stock Vintage
blurb: Serious American workwear and militaria; deadstock denim, chore coats and boots priced for collectors.

name: Cure Thrift Shop
blurb: Nonprofit thrift benefiting diabetes research. Furniture, housewares and clothing under one roof - the most donation-driven shop on this map.

name: Buffalo Exchange
blurb: Buy-sell-trade chain: bring a bag, get cash or store credit on the spot. The easiest place to divert your own clothes.

name: Tokyo Joe
blurb: Designer consignment next door to Buffalo Exchange; steady rotation of contemporary labels at resale prices.

name: Cobblestones
blurb: Small, crowded, and heavy on costume jewelry, beaded bags and earlier-decade pieces.

name: Fabulous Fanny's
blurb: Vintage and antique eyewear specialist - thousands of frames from the 1800s onward. Costume designers shop here.

name: Mr. Throwback
blurb: 1990s sportswear: jerseys, starter jackets, snapbacks, basketball cards.

name: No Relation Vintage
blurb: Part of the L Train Vintage family - high volume, thrift-adjacent pricing, organized by category rather than curated.

name: Rue St. Denis
blurb: Deadstock specialist: never-worn garments from decades past, kept in near-museum condition.

name: Lost City Arts
blurb: Twentieth-century design: industrial lighting, mid-century seating, salvaged signage and architectural pieces.

name: White Trash NYC
blurb: Mid-century furniture and oddball housewares crammed into a narrow storefront.

name: Good Records NYC
blurb: Used vinyl with a careful jazz, soul and reissue selection; buys collections.

name: A1 Record Shop
blurb: Crate-digger's shop - dance, hip-hop, disco and house, plus dollar bins by the door.

name: Gimme Gimme Records
blurb: Used rock, punk and reggae vinyl in a small, well-priced room.

name: East Village Books
blurb: Secondhand books spilling onto the sidewalk; cheap paperbacks and a decent art and poetry section.

name: Mast Books
blurb: Used and out-of-print art, photography and design books, selected with an editor's eye.

name: Alabaster Bookshop
blurb: The last survivor of Book Row - used and rare titles on Fourth Avenue.

name: Strand Book Store
blurb: Eighteen miles of books, a large used and review-copy trade, and a buying desk that takes your old ones.
notes: Just outside the LES/EV line - included as a boundary case

name: Codex Books
blurb: Small, sharply selected used and rare bookshop at the top of the Bowery.

name: David Owens Vintage
blurb: Decades-deep Orchard Street vintage with real depth in early denim, workwear and military.

name: Edith Machinist
blurb: Curated womenswear vintage - slips, boots, bags - with a soft, well-edited feel.

name: Procell
blurb: Archive graphic tees and band shirts at collector prices. As much reference library as shop.

name: Marmalade Vintage
blurb: Affordable general vintage with a party-clothes streak.

name: Sweet Pickle Books
blurb: Used books and house-made pickles - trade a jar for a book. Genuinely one of the odder reuse economies in the city.

name: Bluestockings Cooperative
blurb: Worker-owned radical bookstore and cafe; new and used titles, plus free community programming.

name: James Veloria
blurb: Upstairs in the Elizabeth Center mall - tightly curated designer vintage, strong on 90s Japanese and European labels.

name: Downtown Music Gallery
blurb: Avant-garde, jazz and experimental records, new and used, in a basement under the Manhattan Bridge.

name: Hester Street Fair
blurb: Open-air weekend market with rotating vintage and secondhand vendors. Seasonal - check before you go.

name: Housing Works Bookstore Cafe
blurb: All-donated books and records; every dollar funds Housing Works' services for New Yorkers living with HIV/AIDS and homelessness.

name: INA NY
blurb: Long-standing designer consignment; takes in-season pieces from the public and resells them.
notes: Confirm this location is still open
